DC Queer Bike Rides

Washington, DC · Social

LGBTQ+No-dropBeginner friendly

DC Queer Bike Rides is a social group ride in Washington, DC. It rolls second Saturday of the month at 12:00 pm. About 5–8 miles, social, 5–8 mph. No-drop.

First time? Here's the drill

Bring
a helmet, water, a spare tube or patch kit, a way to pay for the stop.
Arrive
Ten or fifteen minutes before 12:00 pm. Tell whoever's leading that you're new.
Pace
Expect 5–8 mph: you can talk the whole way. It's no-drop: if you fall off the back, someone waits. That's the point of a group ride.
Check
Look at the host's website the day of — that's where cancellations, weather calls and start changes get posted.

About the DC Queer Bike Rides group ride

A sober social ride for queer people in DC. Flat routes, quiet streets, a pace where you can still talk. Start points rotate between spots like Alethia Tanner Park, Fort Totten Metro and the Anacostia River Trail, all near Capital Bikeshare stations. No alcohol, no cops, no transphobes.
